correctness.rationale: Exact two-layer linear dispersion reduces temporal instability to the scalar positive threshold. The Mittag–Leffler expansion gives S(z)=sum c/(z+a); B(z)=-S/S′-z is a weighted mean of a, strictly increasing because -2 Cov(a,(z+a)^-1)>0. It runs from 3M1/M3 to infinity, proving exact zero/one minimizer classification including equality. Differentiating S gives C=12M1M5/(5M3^2)-2>=2/5; analytic inversion proves the positive edge law. Exact symbolic comparison proves distinct capillarity criteria for phase-speed and shear-onset problems. Standalone checker passed randomized and high-precision consistency cases. No part of the infinite-domain proof relies on finite sampling.

value.rationale: The natural physical design task is selecting the first mode destabilized as shear increases between layers of different finite depths. The exact composite moment inequality solves the global mode-selection dichotomy, rules out simultaneous competing interior minima, gives positive square-root and quadratic threshold laws and distinguishes a distinct gravity-capillary phase-speed problem. This is an all-parameter structural classification for unequal depths, not an arbitrary finite computation, tiny numerical improvement, or restatement of the basic dispersion.
